title: Scalable continuous-space crystal optimality certificates
open: Develop computationally practical certificates that a candidate lies within a chosen energy tolerance of the global minimum over continuous atomic positions and variable cell geometry, for a stated class of realistic many-body potentials and bounded cell sizes. Control discretization error explicitly.
status: Gusev et al. demonstrated integer-programming optimality guarantees and assumption-dependent relaxed structures in 2023. Practical scaling, grid-to-continuum error bounds, and wider potential classes remain extension targets.
why: Separates reliable ground-state predictions from search-algorithm preferences.
key_works: Oganov, Pickard, Zhu and Needs (2019), “Structure prediction drives materials discovery,” [DOI:10.1038/s41578-019-0101-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41578-019-0101-8); V. V. Gusev et al. (2023), “Optimality guarantees for crystal structure prediction,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06071-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06071-y).

title: Three-dimensional Kauzmann transition
open: Establish whether realistic three-dimensional glass formers have a thermodynamic ideal-glass transition at positive temperature, with controlled thermodynamic and equilibration limits.
status: Posed in 1948; Jung et al. find a zero-temperature transition in a two-dimensional model, which leaves the three-dimensional question unresolved.
why: Determines whether ordinary glass formation hides an equilibrium phase transition.
key_works: Kauzmann (1948), “The Nature of the Glassy State and the Behavior of Liquids at Low Temperatures,” [DOI:10.1021/cr60135a002](https://doi.org/10.1021/cr60135a002); Jung et al. (2025; journal 2026), “Numerical investigation of the equilibrium Kauzmann transition in a two-dimensional atomistic glass,” [arXiv:2507.03590](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03590).

title: Gardner transition in physical dimensions
open: Determine when the mean-field Gardner transition survives as a true transition in three-dimensional glasses, and distinguish it from a crossover or localized defects.
status: Proposed in spin-glass theory in 1985; mean-field amorphous-solid results and finite-system signatures exist, with dimensional and preparation dependence unresolved.
why: Connects glass stability, anomalous elasticity, and marginality.
key_works: Berthier et al. (2019), “Gardner physics in amorphous solids and beyond,” [DOI:10.1063/1.5097175](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5097175).

title: Chemical identity of tunnelling defects
open: Identify the atomic rearrangements responsible for tunnelling two-level systems in representative amorphous oxides and predict their density and coupling from preparation history.
status: Phenomenological tunnelling models date to the 1970s; individual defects are measurable, but no universal microscopic account spans glass chemistries.
why: Reduces dielectric loss, mechanical noise, and quantum-device decoherence.
key_works: Yu and Carruzzo (2021), “Two-Level Systems and the Tunneling Model: A Critical View,” [arXiv:2101.02787](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.02787).

title: Heat transport beyond weak anharmonicity
open: Predict conductivity in strongly anharmonic, dynamically disordered solids when well-defined phonon quasiparticles and perturbative scattering cease to suffice.
status: Wigner transport unifies particle-like and coherence contributions; strongly nonperturbative, temperature-changing structures remain a demanding frontier.
why: Enables reliable design of complex thermal barriers and thermoelectrics.
key_works: Simoncelli, Marzari and Mauri (2022), “Wigner Formulation of Thermal Transport in Solids,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevX.12.041011](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.12.041011).

title: Atomic tomography of intact buried interfaces
open: Map metal and oxygen atomic positions in three dimensions across an intact buried metal–oxide interface within a micrometre-thick specimen, without sectioning. Establish independently validated atom-recovery, false-assignment, and probe-induced structural-change bounds.
status: Yang et al. mapped 23,196 Fe/Pt atom positions and species in a nanoparticle in 2017; 2021 ptychography reached lattice-vibration-limited resolution. Intact thick mixed-element interfaces impose substantially stronger penetration, inversion, and dose constraints.
why: Measures the actual structures underlying materials properties.
key_works: Y. Yang et al. (2017), “Deciphering chemical order/disorder and material properties at the single-atom level,” [DOI:10.1038/nature21042](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature21042); Chen et al. (2021), “Electron ptychography achieves atomic-resolution limits set by lattice vibrations,” [DOI:10.1126/science.abg2533](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abg2533).

title: Atomic chemistry below the damage threshold
open: Measure local bonding and composition in beam-sensitive materials with independently quantified uncertainty before the probe changes the structure being measured.
status: Low-dose, cryogenic, and dose-fractionated methods mitigate damage; damage-free information acquisition at useful resolution remains specimen dependent.
why: Makes observations of polymers, soft interfaces, and reactive solids trustworthy.
key_works: Egerton (2019), “Radiation damage to organic and inorganic specimens in the TEM,” [DOI:10.1016/j.micron.2019.01.005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.micron.2019.01.005).

title: Identifiable electric-field and strain maps
open: Infer local electric fields and strain from scanning diffraction while separating thickness, tilt, dynamical scattering, probe aberrations, and charging with validated uncertainty.
status: 4D-STEM provides multiple quantitative imaging modes; distinct physical causes can still generate similar measured contrast.
why: Prevents structural or electrostatic artifacts from becoming false mechanism claims.
key_works: Ophus (2019), “Four-Dimensional Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (4D-STEM): From Scanning Nanodiffraction to Ptychography and Beyond,” [DOI:10.1017/S1431927619000497](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1431927619000497).

title: Copper removal from scrap-derived steel at industrial throughput
open: Remove dissolved copper from realistic scrap-steel melts to the specification of demanding sheet products, with demonstrated industrial throughput, iron yield, reagent recycling, and cost competitiveness against dilution with primary iron.
status: Copper accumulation remains a circular-steel bottleneck. Souza Filho et al. demonstrated a promising oxygen-controlled metallurgical removal route in 2024; economically qualified industrial operation across variable scrap streams remains open.
why: Expands high-value steel recycling without continually adding primary iron.
key_works: I. R. Souza Filho et al. (2024), “Sustainable Ironmaking Toward a Future Circular Steel Economy: Exploiting a Critical Oxygen Concentration for Metallurgical Cu Removal from Scrap-Based Melts,” [DOI:10.1002/srin.202300785](https://doi.org/10.1002/srin.202300785).

title: Site-resolved martensite nucleation under deformation
open: Predict which measured defects nucleate martensite, the selected crystallographic variants, and onset stresses in metastable stainless steel across temperature and strain-rate changes, without prescribing embryos from the eventual observed microstructure.
status: Atomic observations and simulations in 316L at 15 and 173 K identified different transformation pathways and defect associations in 2025; prospectively selecting actual nucleation sites remains harder than explaining observed ones.
why: Makes transformation-induced strengthening and ductility more reliably designable.
key_works: S. Li, P. J. Withers, W. Chen, K. Yan (2025), “Atomic-scale investigation of the mechanisms of deformation-induced martensitic transformation at ultra-cryogenic temperatures,” [DOI:10.1016/j.jmst.2024.04.067](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmst.2024.04.067).

title: Closure of three-dimensional dislocation-network dynamics
open: Obtain tractable continuum evolution equations that preserve dislocation topology and predict multiplication, junction formation, annihilation, and pattern length scales from initial microstructure, without regime-specific fitted closure rules.
status: Phase-field formulations with conserved dislocation variables demonstrated pattern formation in 2025; deriving broadly valid correlation and reaction closures remains distinct from demonstrating selected patterns.
why: Connects microscopic dislocation motion to component-scale constitutive models.
key_works: Y. Zhang, R. Wu, M. Zaiser (2025), “Continuum dislocation dynamics as a phase field theory with conserved order parameters: formulation and application to dislocation patterning,” [DOI:10.1088/1361-651X/adc31f](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-651X/adc31f); [arXiv:2410.17177](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17177).

title: Slip transmission through chemically complex grain boundaries
open: Predict whether an incident dislocation is absorbed, transmitted, or re-emitted at a measured three-dimensional boundary, including its segregation state and local stress, and validate the outgoing slip system in situ.
status: Stricker and Weygand implemented explicit transmission through planar boundaries in 2024. Curved, chemically heterogeneous boundaries and evolving boundary dislocation content extend beyond that controlled setting.
why: Connects grain-boundary design to strain localization and crack initiation.
key_works: M. Stricker and D. Weygand (2024), “A model for physical dislocation transmission through grain boundaries and its implementation in a discrete dislocation dynamics tool,” [DOI:10.1186/s41313-024-00065-7](https://doi.org/10.1186/s41313-024-00065-7).

title: Hydrogen-trap protection after saturation and cycling
open: Determine when deliberately introduced traps remain protective under repeated charging, unloading, and temperature cycling, versus saturating or releasing hydrogen into crack-critical regions; demonstrate predictive limits for actual microstructures.
status: Atomic-scale trapping measurements and interface-engineering strategies exist. A reduction in initial hydrogen uptake, including the approximately twofold reduction reported by Hachet et al., does not establish lifetime protection.
why: Prevents mitigation strategies from failing after apparently successful short tests.
key_works: G. Hachet et al. (2025), “Protection of metal interfaces against hydrogen-assisted cracking,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67310-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67310-6).

title: Material-specific onset of dynamic crack microbranching
open: Predict the onset velocity, branch spacing, and three-dimensional morphology of dynamic microbranching from independently measured dissipation and process-zone physics across brittle material classes.
status: Controlled experiments established microbranching in the 1990s; contemporary simulations generate branching, but reproducing it does not by itself validate transferable onset and length-scale predictions.
why: Determines rapid-fracture resistance and fragmentation beyond quasistatic toughness.
key_works: E. Sharon, S. P. Gross, J. Fineberg (1995), “Local crack branching as a mechanism for instability in dynamic fracture,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.5096](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.5096); E. Sharon and J. Fineberg (1996), “Microbranching instability and the dynamic fracture of brittle materials,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.54.7128](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.54.7128).

title: Preventing keyhole pores by closed-loop control
open: Detect incipient keyhole instability and adjust the laser before pore entrapment across scan turns, accumulated heat, and changing surface angles, demonstrating lower defect rates on entire builds with measured false-alarm rates.
status: A 2025 acoustic study correlated frequency signatures with keyhole depth and porosity onset across several alloys. Generalized prevention requires control action and full-build validation beyond detection.
why: Prevents internal defects during manufacture and reduces dependence on later inspection.
key_works: L. Galiègue et al. (2025), “Acoustic emission monitoring reveals keyhole formation and evolution,” [DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-27232-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-27232-1).

title: Oxidation-tolerant crack-deflecting CMC interphases
subfield: Structural ceramics, ceramic composites, and refractories
open: Design a fiber–matrix interphase that remains sufficiently weak for crack deflection and fiber pull-out while resisting oxidation and volatilization through service-induced matrix cracks.
status: SiC/BN/SiBCN studies in 2025 show that steam can consume BN and form glassy products that bond fibers to the matrix. Initial toughness therefore does not guarantee retained toughness after exposure.
why: Preserves the damage tolerance that makes ceramic-matrix composites useful.
key_works: Z. Li, Z. Gao, X. Zhang, Y. Liu, P. J. Withers, P. Xiao (2025), “Oxidation behavior and subsequent mechanical properties of SiC/BN/SiBCN composite after exposure to steam at high temperature,” [institutional paper record](https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/publications/oxidation-behavior-and-subsequent-mechanical-properties-of-sicbns/).

title: Rapid uniform densification of thick CMC preforms
subfield: Structural ceramics, ceramic composites, and refractories
open: Achieve a specified near-full matrix density throughout thick, complex fiber preforms in a single short infiltration campaign without prematurely sealing outer pores or damaging fibers, verified by three-dimensional porosity and mechanical measurements.
status: Venkatachalam et al. reported 90% theoretical density in 24 hours using radio-frequency-assisted CVI in 2024, at least ten times faster than their conventional comparison. Higher density, complex geometry, and validated properties remain separate hurdles.
why: Reduces a major time and cost barrier in ceramic-composite manufacturing.
key_works: V. Venkatachalam, B. Esser, J. Binner (2024), “Processing and performance of ultra high temperature ceramic matrix composite (UHTCMCs) using radio frequency assisted chemical vapour infiltration (RF-CVI),” [DLR paper record](https://elib.dlr.de/205288/).

title: Repeated autonomous concrete healing with structural recovery
subfield: Cement, concrete, earthen materials, and glass durability
open: Demonstrate repeated crack healing that restores specified permeability and mechanical performance after multiple damage events under realistic wet–dry exposure, without exhausting healing capacity or causing harmful expansion.
status: Seymour et al.’s 2023 experiments support lime-clast-mediated healing inspired by Roman concrete. Repeatable recovery in reinforced structural service remains beyond one-time laboratory crack closure.
why: Reduces repair needs and extends material service life.
key_works: L. M. Seymour et al. (2023), “Hot mixing: Mechanistic insights into the durability of ancient Roman concrete,” [DOI:10.1126/sciadv.add1602](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.add1602).

title: Operando accounting of inactive lithium
open: Quantify, spatially and during operation, lithium lost to electronically isolated metal separately from lithium bound in interphase products, without perturbing the buried electrode. Close the lithium mass balance in realistic multilayer cells.
status: Fang et al. introduced destructive titration–gas chromatography in 2019. Later imaging and recovery studies establish that isolated lithium can move or reconnect; a generally applicable operando inventory remains a distinct target.
why: Identifies which loss process an electrolyte or charging intervention actually fixes.
key_works: C. Fang et al. (2019), “Quantifying inactive lithium in lithium metal batteries,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1481-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1481-z).

title: Stripping-induced void suppression at solid–lithium interfaces
open: Prevent contact loss when lithium is removed faster than interfacial creep and diffusion can replenish it, at useful current and capacity with low external pressure. Predict the safe operating window from measured interface properties.
status: Kasemchainan et al. directly connected stripping-current limits, voids, and subsequent dendrites in 2019. Pressure and interlayers mitigate particular interfaces; transferable criteria across electrolyte, temperature, and lithium thickness remain incomplete.
why: Addresses a failure mechanism that can precede short circuits even when plating initially appears uniform.
key_works: J. Kasemchainan et al. (2019), “Critical stripping current leads to dendrite formation on plating in lithium anode solid electrolyte cells,” [DOI:10.1038/s41563-019-0438-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-019-0438-9).

title: Reversible oxygen redox without cumulative voltage loss
open: Obtain substantial anionic-redox capacity while avoiding oxygen release, irreversible cation rearrangement, and accumulating charge–discharge hysteresis over practical cycling. Identify structural rules that work across compositions rather than one special material.
status: Oxygen-redox cathodes have been developed for decades. House et al. demonstrated superstructure control of first-cycle hysteresis in 2020; first-cycle improvements do not by themselves establish stable lifetime energy efficiency.
why: Unlocks cathode capacity beyond transition-metal redox without sacrificing delivered energy.
key_works: R. A. House et al. (2020), “Superstructure control of first-cycle voltage hysteresis in oxygen-redox cathodes,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1854-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1854-3).

title: Magnesium interfaces compatible with high-energy full cells
open: Create an electronically passivating yet Mg-ion-conducting interface that supports efficient metal cycling and a high-voltage, high-loading cathode in the same electrolyte, including realistic impurity tolerance.
status: Son et al. demonstrated an artificial interphase enabling reversible magnesium chemistry in carbonate electrolyte in 2018. This resolves a proof-of-principle incompatibility; a broadly practical cathode–electrolyte–anode combination remains unfinished.
why: Allows abundant magnesium to compete on full-cell energy and cost.
key_works: S.-B. Son et al. (2018), “An artificial interphase enables reversible magnesium chemistry in carbonate electrolytes,” [DOI:10.1038/s41557-018-0019-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-018-0019-6).

title: Regenerable organic flow-battery molecules
open: Design inexpensive redox molecules whose dominant degradation products can be returned to active material in situ with little energy or reagent consumption, without accumulating irreversible contaminants.
status: Organic-electrolyte decomposition has constrained the field for years. Jing et al. demonstrated electrochemical recomposition of a decomposed anthraquinone electrolyte in 2022; broadly applicable regeneration across both electrolytes and repeated aging remains open.
why: Makes electrolyte lifetime repairable instead of requiring continual chemical replacement.
key_works: Y. Jing et al. (2022), “In situ electrochemical recomposition of decomposed redox-active species in aqueous organic flow batteries,” [DOI:10.1038/s41557-022-00967-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-022-00967-4).

title: Singlet-oxygen-resistant lithium–oxygen chemistry
open: Suppress or harmlessly quench singlet oxygen during oxygen reduction and evolution without sacrificing useful capacity or adding consumable scavengers. Demonstrate closed oxygen and electrolyte mass balances over extended cycling.
status: Mahne et al. identified singlet oxygen as a major parasitic-reaction source in 2017. Quenchers and mediator redesign help individual pathways, but reversible aprotic oxygen cycling with durable components remains unresolved.
why: Addresses chemical destruction that otherwise masquerades as rechargeable oxygen capacity.
key_works: N. Mahne et al. (2017), “Singlet oxygen generation as a major cause for parasitic reactions during cycling of aprotic lithium–oxygen batteries,” [DOI:10.1038/nenergy.2017.36](https://doi.org/10.1038/nenergy.2017.36).

title: Lead immobilization through damage and end of life
open: Develop lead-binding materials that retain released lead after realistic breakage, weathering, and disposal exposures, while permitting efficient module recycling. Quantify capture saturation and leaching products rather than only intact-module leakage.
status: Adsorption, complexation, grain isolation, and encapsulation approaches were assessed comprehensively in 2023. The unresolved target is durable containment across failure modes with demonstrated recovery, not merely the existence of lead sorbents.
why: Reduces environmental release and simplifies responsible deployment of lead-containing absorbers.
key_works: H. Zhang et al. (2023), “Lead immobilization for environmentally sustainable perovskite solar cells,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-05938-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-05938-4).

title: Useful bulk p-type conductivity in beta-gallium oxide
open: Demonstrate reproducible, mobile-hole conduction in bulk beta-Ga2O3 at device-useful temperatures and densities, with compensation and parasitic phases excluded; alternatively establish the material-specific limits imposed by self-trapping and acceptor energetics.
status: Self-trapped holes were identified as a fundamental obstacle by Varley and colleagues in 2012. Reports of p-type behavior require distinguishing band transport from defect, surface, and secondary-phase conduction.
why: Would enable native bipolar architectures in an ultrawide-bandgap power material.
key_works: J. B. Varley, A. Janotti, C. Franchini and C. G. Van de Walle (2012), “Role of self-trapping in luminescence and p-type conductivity of wide-band-gap oxides,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.85.081109](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.85.081109).

title: Efficient room-temperature electron doping of diamond
open: Introduce electrically active donors into device-quality diamond with sufficiently shallow activation, low compensation, and controlled spatial profiles to support low-resistance room-temperature electron transport.
status: Diamond n-type doping has been pursued for decades and is not wholly absent: phosphorus-doped material exists. The 2025 review emphasizes deep levels, incorporation limitations, and room-temperature conductivity as continuing obstacles.
why: Complements diamond's established hole conduction for high-power bipolar devices.
key_works: M. Sultana, S. Karmakar and A. Haque (2025), [“N- and P-type doping of diamonds: A review”](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S136980012400920X).

title: High-conductivity p-type aluminum nitride
open: Achieve stable, reproducible hole injection and conduction in high-quality AlN without excessive compensation, optical absorption, or contact resistance. Validate the mechanism in functioning AlN-based bipolar structures.
status: Deep acceptors have constrained AlN devices for decades. Ma et al. reported Mg-doped p-type films in 2025, while identifying limited activation and mobility; detecting p-type character does not settle useful device conductivity.
why: Supports deep-ultraviolet emitters and ultrawide-bandgap bipolar electronics.
key_works: Y. Ma et al. (2025), “Mg-Doped P-Type AlN Thin Film Prepared by Magnetron Sputtering Using Mg-Al Alloy Targets,” [DOI:10.3390/mi16091035](https://doi.org/10.3390/mi16091035).

title: Wafer-scale 2D single crystals without stitched-boundary penalties
open: Grow device-grade monolayers with uniform thickness, orientation, and defect density over manufacturing wafers, avoiding electrically harmful translation boundaries where aligned domains merge. Establish reproducible yield across batches and substrates.
status: Jiang et al. demonstrated centimetre-scale single-domain MoS2 through two-dimensional Czochralski growth in 2025. Extending single-domain quality to manufacturing-scale wafers and compatible substrates remains open.
why: Makes large-area two-dimensional electronics predictable at the individual-device level.
key_works: H. Jiang et al. (2025), “Two-dimensional Czochralski growth of single-crystal MoS2,” [DOI:10.1038/s41563-024-02069-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-024-02069-7).

title: Continuous electrically pumped colloidal-quantum-dot lasing
open: Demonstrate sustained electrically pumped lasing with clear cavity-mode and coherence evidence, while controlling Auger recombination, charge imbalance, Joule heating, and optical loss in a solution-processable quantum-dot device.
status: Ahn et al. achieved electrically driven amplified spontaneous emission in 2023. That milestone establishes electrical gain, while continuous laser operation and durable devices impose additional materials constraints.
why: Enables chemically tunable, integrated laser sources fabricated from colloidal materials.
key_works: N. Ahn et al. (2023), “Electrically driven amplified spontaneous emission from colloidal quantum dots,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-05855-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-05855-6).

title: The superconducting order parameter of Sr2RuO4
open: Identify an order parameter consistent with spin susceptibility, strain response, time-reversal-symmetry tests, gap structure, and thermodynamics in comparably characterized samples, resolving conflicting interpretations among these probes.
status: Unsettled since superconductivity was discovered in 1994. Pustogow et al.'s 2019 oxygen-NMR results challenged the long-favored spin-triplet interpretation; a universally consistent experimental identification remains open.
why: Tests how multiorbital electronic correlations create unconventional superconductivity.
key_works: A. Pustogow et al. (2019), “Constraints on the superconducting order parameter in Sr2RuO4 from oxygen-17 nuclear magnetic resonance,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1596-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1596-2).

title: Arbitrary-sequence synthetic polymers at production scale
open: Produce nonbiological-backbone polymers with long, individually specified monomer sequences while controlling chain length, stereochemistry, and sequence defects. A demanding census target is kilogram batches of prescribed 1,000-unit chains with independently measured whole-chain sequence fidelity above 99%.
status: Sequence control has advanced substantially since the 2000s through iterative synthesis, controlled polymerization, and biological templates; these capabilities do not establish this combined length–fidelity–throughput target for arbitrary synthetic backbones.
why: Enables reproducible synthetic catalysts, molecular information storage, and protein-like materials with new chemistries.
key_works: J.-F. Lutz, M. Ouchi, D. R. Liu, and M. Sawamoto (2013), “Sequence-Controlled Polymers,” [DOI:10.1126/science.1238149](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1238149); J.-F. Lutz (2017), “Defining the Field of Sequence-Controlled Polymers,” [DOI:10.1002/marc.201700582](https://doi.org/10.1002/marc.201700582).

title: Repeated autonomous restoration of elastomer fatigue resistance
open: Restore a damaged elastomer’s fatigue threshold repeatedly at ambient conditions, including contaminated interfaces and sustained load, without losing dimensional stability. Demonstrating tensile-strength recovery alone does not establish restoration of resistance to cyclic crack growth.
status: Self-healing has progressed from soft networks to stiff composites; Liu et al. reported an approximately 8.23 kJ/m² fatigue threshold and rapid near-infrared-triggered healing in 2025. Autonomous repair under realistic continuing service remains a stronger combined target.
why: Enables repairable load-bearing soft components with measurable service-life gains.
key_works: T. Liu et al. (2025), “Multiscale interlinked structures limit fatigue crack propagation in a MXene-polyurethane composite,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64611-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64611-8).

title: Device-quality colloidal diamond
subfield: Colloids, liquid crystals, gels, and active soft materials
open: Assemble large, orientationally controlled colloidal-diamond domains with sufficiently low vacancy, stacking, and grain-boundary defect densities for a specified complete photonic bandgap. Preserve the architecture during conversion into a useful high-index material and demonstrate reproducible optical performance.
status: Colloidal diamond itself was experimentally assembled by He et al. in 2020 after decades of effort; scalable, defect-controlled assembly plus device-material conversion is the remaining integrated problem.
why: Offers an inexpensive route to three-dimensional photonic materials.

title: Inverse design of assembly pathways
subfield: Colloids, liquid crystals, gels, and active soft materials
open: Given a target colloidal structure and practical interactions, find a temperature, concentration, or field protocol that maximizes finite-time yield while avoiding competing structures. The method must predict kinetic failures, not only identify a favorable equilibrium phase.
status: Established by the 2010s as a distinct problem; simulations and selected controlled protocols outperform fixed conditions, but transferable inverse design for realistic hydrodynamics and polydispersity remains limited.
why: Makes self-assembly a reliable manufacturing method for complex structures.
key_works: S. Whitelam and R. L. Jack (2015), “The Statistical Mechanics of Dynamic Pathways to Self-Assembly,” [DOI:10.1146/annurev-physchem-040214-121215](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-physchem-040214-121215); W. M. Jacobs, A. Reinhardt, and D. Frenkel (2015), “Rational design of self-assembly pathways for complex multicomponent structures,” [arXiv:1502.01351](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.01351).

title: Predicting the foreign-body response from material design
open: Predict long-term capsule formation and inflammatory cell states from material chemistry, mechanics, geometry, implantation site, and host condition. A successful model must generalize across species and distinguish surgical injury effects from material-induced immune responses.
status: Studied for decades; material size and shape affect responses, and adhesive interfaces prevented observable capsules for 12 weeks in several animal settings in 2024. General host- and site-transferable prediction remains open.
why: Reduces failure of implants, biosensors, and drug-delivery devices.
key_works: O. Veiseh et al. (2015), “Size- and shape-dependent foreign body immune response to materials implanted in rodents and non-human primates,” [DOI:10.1038/nmat4290](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat4290); J. Wu et al. (2024), “Adhesive anti-fibrotic interfaces on diverse organs,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07426-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07426-9).

title: Long-lived small-diameter vascular grafts
open: Produce readily available small-diameter grafts that maintain physiological compliance, endothelial function, and patency without progressive thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, or aneurysm. Confirm long-term performance in anatomically and hemodynamically demanding graft configurations and comparative human studies.
status: A decades-old challenge; Zhang et al. reported 100% patency in their allogeneic rhesus-macaque experiment in 2025. That study-specific result does not establish universal or multiyear clinical durability.
why: Provides vascular replacements when suitable autologous vessels are unavailable.
key_works: J. Zhang et al. (2025), “Small-diameter artery grafts engineered from pluripotent stem cells maintain 100% patency in an allogeneic rhesus macaque model,” [DOI:10.1016/j.xcrm.2025.102002](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2025.102002).

title: Defined dynamic matrices across organoid lineages
open: Replace variable animal-derived matrices with chemically defined materials that support reproducible expansion, differentiation, and maturation across specified human organoid lineages. Determine which time-dependent mechanical and ligand changes are necessary for each developmental transition.
status: Gjorevski et al. demonstrated dynamic synthetic matrices for intestinal organoids in 2016; later matrices extend selected tissue systems. A transferable recipe covering diverse lineages and mature function remains open.
why: Improves reproducibility of disease models, drug testing, and tissue manufacture.
key_works: N. Gjorevski et al. (2016), “Designer matrices for intestinal stem cell and organoid culture,” [DOI:10.1038/nature20168](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature20168).

title: Practical broadband three-dimensional elastic cloaking
open: Reduce scattering of both longitudinal and shear elastic waves over a specified finite band and range of incidence using finite, manufacturable material parameters. Include support loads, losses, and imperfections in the demonstrated performance specification.
status: Transformation elasticity gives exact idealized designs, and restricted-wave demonstrations exist. Simultaneous three-dimensional, multipolarization, broadband performance under practical constitutive constraints remains unresolved; unlimited perfect passive cloaking is not the target.
why: Enables vibration protection and unobtrusive structural supports.
key_works: A. N. Norris and A. L. Shuvalov (2011), “Elastic cloaking theory,” [arXiv:1103.6045](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.6045).

title: Active metasurfaces with joint efficiency, speed, and endurance
open: Produce addressable metasurface materials with large reversible optical modulation while jointly meeting useful switching speed, low loss, low energy, and high cycle life over a large area. Report aging and pixel-to-pixel drift alongside the initial optical response.
status: Electrical, thermal, mechanical, and phase-change tuning are established; the speed, modulation depth, loss, and integration tradeoffs identified in 2019 continue to motivate distinct material platforms. No single tuning mechanism settles the combined specification.
why: Enables practical dynamic holography, beam steering, and adaptive optics.
key_works: A. M. Shaltout, V. M. Shalaev, and M. L. Brongersma (2019), “Spatiotemporal light control with active metasurfaces,” [DOI:10.1126/science.aat3100](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat3100).

title: Chemistry-based closure of moving-contact-line dynamics
subfield: Surfaces, wetting, adhesion, and functional coatings
open: Predict a moving liquid contact line from independently measured surface chemistry and molecular dynamics, including speed-dependent contact angle and transitions to film deposition. Bridge microscopic slip, adsorption, and contact-line friction to macroscopic flow without refitting an effective parameter for each experiment.
status: Slip and diffuse-interface models regularize the classical moving-contact-line singularity. The 2013 review by Snoeijer and Andreotti documents established regimes and remaining microscopic-to-continuum matching questions; real heterogeneous surfaces add unresolved history dependence.
why: Makes coating, printing, immersion lithography, and fluid deposition quantitatively predictable.
key_works: J. H. Snoeijer and B. Andreotti (2013), “Moving Contact Lines: Scales, Regimes, and Dynamical Transitions,” [DOI:10.1146/annurev-fluid-011212-140734](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-fluid-011212-140734).

title: Long-lived submerged gas layers on superhydrophobic surfaces
subfield: Surfaces, wetting, adhesion, and functional coatings
open: Sustain a useful gas-covered fraction under specified water depth, gas undersaturation, turbulence, abrasion, and contamination for the intended service interval. Predict when gas dissolution or wetting nucleation causes failure, and quantify any gas-replenishment energy.
status: Jones et al. connected roughness scale to submerged gas/vapor stability in 2015. Thermodynamic stability arguments and laboratory plastron retention do not alone establish durability under combined field conditions.
why: Makes submerged drag reduction and corrosion isolation more dependable.
key_works: P. R. Jones et al. (2015), “Sustaining dry surfaces under water,” [DOI:10.1038/srep12311](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep12311).

title: Catalyst-tolerant processing of dirty mixed plastic waste
open: Process changing mixtures of polymers, dyes, stabilizers, fillers, food residues, and halogen-containing contaminants while retaining catalyst activity and useful product selectivity. Establish quantitative contaminant tolerance limits and regenerability using representative waste, rather than only model mixtures.
status: Sullivan et al. combined chemical oxidation and biological funneling for mixed plastics in 2022. Sustained operation under realistic impurity distributions, separation demands, and feed changes remains a distinct scale-up problem.
why: Reduces expensive presorting and avoids exporting contamination into recycled products.
key_works: K. P. Sullivan et al. (2022), “Mixed plastics waste valorization through tandem chemical oxidation and biological funneling,” [DOI:10.1126/science.abo4626](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abo4626).

title: Predicting resumption of waste-glass alteration
subfield: Radiation, nuclear materials, and extreme environments
open: Determine when secondary-phase formation destabilizes a protective alteration layer and accelerates nuclear-waste-glass dissolution. Predict induction times and acceleration magnitudes under independently specified water chemistry, temperature, and surface-area conditions.
status: Forty years of standardized durability testing are reviewed in 2021; alteration resumption is observed in some conditions and absent in others, preventing its treatment as a universal fixed stage.
why: Identifies conditions that could invalidate simple long-term durability extrapolations.
key_works: C. L. Thorpe et al. (2021), “Forty years of durability assessment of nuclear waste glass by standard methods,” [DOI:10.1038/s41529-021-00210-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-021-00210-4).

title: Phason-entropy stabilization of decagonal Al–Co–Cu
open: Determine whether, and by how much, phason entropy stabilizes decagonal Al–Co–Cu relative to crystalline approximants in the converged quasiperiodic limit. Separate phason, chemical, and vibrational entropy, then predict the equilibrium stability window without fitting its transition temperature.
status: Huang, Widom, and Mihalkovič’s 2024 calculations place their quasicrystal approximants at least about 3 meV per atom above crystalline competitors at zero temperature and predict entropy stabilization around 600–800 K. Experimental validation remains open; 2025 ground-state calculations for other binary quasicrystals also show why entropy stabilization should not be assumed universal.
why: It would establish which microscopic disorder stabilizes a real quasiperiodic solid and make its thermal processing predictable.
key_works: Y. Huang, M. Widom, and M. Mihalkovič (2024), “Simulated structure and thermodynamics of decagonal Al-Co-Cu quasicrystals,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.033145](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevResearch.6.033145); W. Baek et al. (2025), “Quasicrystal stability and nucleation kinetics from density functional theory,” [DOI:10.1038/s41567-025-02925-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-025-02925-6).

title: Same-specimen reconciliation of MXene hydroxyl assignments
open: Determine genuine hydroxyl termination abundance and geometry on Ti₃C₂Tₓ separately from intercalated water, adsorbed water, and oxidation products. Reconcile isotope-sensitive solid-state NMR and photoelectron spectroscopy on matched specimens with controlled hydration histories and a closed hydrogen inventory.
status: A 2020 NMR–DFT study assigned terminating hydroxyls and distinct water environments. A 2021 UPS/XPS study concluded that hydroxyls were not inherent terminations of its Ti₃C₂Tₓ surfaces. Reconciling these assignments through measured preparation and measurement histories remains open.
why: Surface proton identity changes interfacial reactions, ion binding, and the interpretation of computational MXene models.
key_works: T. Kobayashi et al. (2020), “Nature of Terminating Hydroxyl Groups and Intercalating Water in Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXenes: A Study by ¹H Solid-State NMR and DFT Calculations,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpcc.0c04744](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcc.0c04744); L.-Å. Näslund et al. (2021), “Chemical Bonding of Termination Species in 2D Carbides Investigated through Valence Band UPS/XPS of Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene,” [DOI:10.1088/2053-1583/ac1ea9](https://doi.org/10.1088/2053-1583/ac1ea9).

title: Prescribing zeolite aluminum sites and aluminum pairs
open: Synthesize a zeolite with a specified distribution of aluminum among inequivalent tetrahedral sites and a specified population of aluminum pairs, while holding framework topology and bulk Si/Al ratio fixed. Prospectively select site populations and pair separations rather than only measuring them afterward.
status: This longstanding synthesis-control problem became more sharply measurable through Rzepka et al.’s 2025 anomalous X-ray diffraction determination of aluminum distributions in ZSM-5. Site mapping is a major advance, but it does not provide arbitrary control over occupancy, pairing, or redistribution during later treatment.
why: Identical bulk compositions can contain different acid-site arrangements and support different catalytic pathways.
key_works: P. Rzepka et al. (2025), “Aluminum distribution and active site locations in the structures of zeolite ZSM-5 catalysts,” [DOI:10.1126/science.ads7290](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ads7290).

title: Strong intrinsic argon-over-oxygen recognition
open: Design an ambient-temperature physisorbent strongly favoring argon over oxygen while retaining reversible uptake. A proposed census target is Ar/O₂ selectivity of at least ten at 298–310 K and at least 0.5 mmol g⁻¹ argon working capacity between 1 and 0.1 bar; these are proposed thresholds, not community benchmarks.
status: Yan et al.’s 2025 MOF reports selectivity around 1.4 and argon uptake around 10 cm³ g⁻¹ at 308 K and 1 bar. Zhao et al. already demonstrate oxygen product purity above 99.99% with AlFUM; purity must be distinguished from recovery yield.
why: Stronger recognition could reduce sorbent inventories and gas-recycling burdens.
key_works: F. Yan et al. (2025), “An amino-functionalized ultra-micropore metal–organic framework using for argon/oxygen adsorption separation,” [DOI:10.1016/j.jiec.2025.01.013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jiec.2025.01.013); S. Zhao et al. (2025), “Selective recognition of argon by an aluminum-based MOF for oxygen recovery from Ar/O₂ mixture under ambient conditions,” [DOI:10.1016/j.ces.2025.122130](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ces.2025.122130).

title: GeTe resistance drift beyond a single structural-relaxation clock
open: Identify the microscopic processes producing both temperature-independent early drift and accelerated late drift in melt-quenched GeTe. Predict resistance from 10 ns to 1,000 s across temperature and quench rate, including increased drift coefficients after slower quenching.
status: Ballmaier, Walfort, and Salinga’s 2025 measurements span eleven time decades and approximately room temperature to 460 K. Submicrosecond behavior and late acceleration near the glass transition depart from familiar power-law models; the authors identify deficiencies in existing descriptions.
why: Predictive drift physics would improve analog-memory reliability and distinguish stable states from short observation windows.
key_works: J. Ballmaier, S. Walfort, and M. Salinga (2025), “Resistance Drift of Phase Change Materials Beyond the Power Law,” [DOI:10.1002/aelm.202400905](https://doi.org/10.1002/aelm.202400905).

title: Stable coherent NV centres within two nanometres of diamond surfaces
open: Demonstrate a nitrogen-vacancy centre 0.5–2 nm below a diamond surface that retains its useful charge state and the coherence protection predicted for surface-induced strain plus a weak static magnetic field. Independently establish depth and the surface electric- and magnetic-noise spectra.
status: Pershin et al.’s 2025 first-principles study proposes protection even near 1 nm depth, but favorable limits assume strong isotopic purification and sufficiently weak electric-field noise. Coherence demonstrations at larger shallow depths do not establish this ultrasmall stand-off regime.
why: This distance regime would strengthen coupling to individual external nuclear spins and molecular-scale magnetic structure.
key_works: A. Pershin, A. Tárkányi, V. Verkhovlyuk, V. Ivády, and A. Gali (2025), “A coherence-protection scheme for quantum sensors based on ultra-shallow single nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64771-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64771-7).

title: Experimental Purcell refrigeration below the rare-earth thermal-population limit
open: Demonstrate net laser refrigeration below liquid-nitrogen temperature using a cavity that preferentially enhances higher-energy fluorescence from a rare-earth-doped crystal. Include parasitic absorption, surface quenching, optical escape, and a calibrated heat load in the demonstration.
status: Ju et al.’s 2026 calculation uses measured Yb:YLF coefficients and predicts approximately 38 K for a nanocrystal near a cavity, compared with an experimental rare-earth refrigeration baseline of 87 K cited in that work. The lower temperature is a theoretical projection.
why: This regime could extend vibration-free optical refrigeration to detectors and quantum devices needing deeper cryogenic cooling.
key_works: P. Ju et al. (2026), “Purcell-enhanced optical refrigeration,” [DOI:10.1103/d7pk-hsry](https://doi.org/10.1103/d7pk-hsry), [arXiv:2404.19142](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19142).

title: Distinguishing bulk-flexoelectric boundary layers from surface piezoelectricity
open: Design a measurement separating genuine surface piezoelectricity from surface-localized response generated by bulk flexoelectricity. Independently vary sample size, surface termination, and electrical boundary conditions while resolving strain or field profiles.
status: Mohammadi et al.’s 2025 closed-form solutions show that finite flexoelectric bodies can respond near surfaces even under homogeneous loading. Such boundary layers resemble surface piezoelectric effects, creating an experimental attribution problem; the continuum boundary-layer calculation itself is already solved.
why: Reliable attribution is needed before large nanoscale coupling coefficients can be transferred to devices or used to infer symmetry.
key_works: H. Mohammadi, F. Greco, D. Codony, and I. Arias (2025), “Flexoelectricity causes surface piezoelectric-like effects in dielectrics,” [DOI:10.1016/j.ijmecsci.2025.110162](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijmecsci.2025.110162), [arXiv:2501.17626](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17626).

title: Three-dimensional trap geography in SrAl₂O₄:Eu,Dy afterglow
open: Determine the spatial distribution and connectivity of Eu emitters, Dy electron traps, and competing defects, then predict charging, afterglow, and thermoluminescence from that measured structure. Avoid separately refitting arbitrary trap-energy distributions or hopping networks to each experiment.
status: Optical work published in 2025 directly supports trapping at lanthanide codopants, including Dy. Koizumi et al.’s 2025 random-walk model reproduces several luminescence processes using an inferred one-dimensional trap landscape; connecting these effective models to independently measured three-dimensional geometry remains open.
why: It would make brightness, charging speed, and persistence jointly designable.
key_works: D. Van der Heggen, J. J. Joos, and P. F. Smet (2025), “Optical Evidence of Charge Trapping at Lanthanide Codopants in SrAl₂O₄:Eu,Ln (Ln = Nd, Sm, Dy) Persistent Phosphors,” [DOI:10.1002/adom.202402153](https://doi.org/10.1002/adom.202402153); R. Koizumi et al. (2025), “Visualization of trap distribution in SrAl₂O₄:Eu²⁺,Dy³⁺ … based on a random walk model,” [DOI:10.1039/D5CP01232E](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5CP01232E).

title: Linear-contamination threshold in ring-melt viscosity
open: Determine the linear-chain concentration creating a rubbery plateau or dominating zero-shear viscosity as a function of both ring and contaminant molecular weights. Recover intrinsic ring-melt viscosity with quantified uncertainty below the relevant contamination threshold.
status: The 2024 reassessment of moderately entangled ring melts identifies remaining purity and analytical-detection limits as obstacles to accurate viscosity measurements. Trace linear chains can obscure the terminal response precisely where competing descriptions of ring relaxation need stringent tests.
why: A calibrated threshold would make ring-rheology measurements comparable and prevent impurity-controlled relaxation from being mistaken for intrinsic topology.
key_works: K. Peponaki, D. Tsalikis, N. Patelis, G. Sakellariou, T. Chang, and D. Vlassopoulos (2024), “Revisiting the Viscosity of Moderately Entangled Ring Polymer Melts,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.macromol.4c00601](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.macromol.4c00601).

title: Experimental realization of colloidal-ring topological bigels
open: Realize the predicted bicomponent gel of polymers threaded through colloidal rings and measure its ring-radius threshold, connectivity, and terminal rheology. Show that network lifetime follows threading constraints rather than uncontrolled attractive aggregation.
status: Bonato, Marenduzzo, and Orlandini’s 2025 simulations predict a fluid-to-gel-like transition above a critical ring radius, with an analytical threshold estimate and slowed entanglement mobility. Experimental realization and finite-lifetime limits remain the next tests.
why: Such gels could obtain connectivity from removable geometric constraints without permanent cross-links.
key_works: A. Bonato, D. Marenduzzo, and E. Orlandini (2025), “Formation of Topological Bigels in Mixtures of Colloidal Rings and Polymers,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.188203](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.188203).

title: Predicting knot-specific mechanochemical scission
open: Predict how knot type, tightness, and backbone chemistry jointly determine polymer-chain scission location and force-dependent rate. Compare knot topologies and unknotted controls with matched chemical linkages and loading histories.
status: Zhang et al. demonstrated mechanical weakening by a molecular knot in 2024. That resolves the basic existence question for their architecture but does not provide a transferable law distinguishing geometric stress concentration, knot friction, and intrinsic bond reactivity.
why: Molecular knots could become predictable mechanophores rather than uncontrolled weak points.
key_works: M. Zhang, R. Nixon, F. Schaufelberger, L. Pirvu, G. De Bo, and D. A. Leigh (2024), “Mechanical scission of a knotted polymer,” [DOI:10.1038/s41557-024-01510-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-024-01510-3).

title: Autophobic dewetting versus core–ligand chemical mismatch
open: Separate matrix-chain entropy, particle curvature, and core–ligand chemical mismatch as causes of demixing in polymer-grafted nanoparticles. Predict whether increasing the matrix-to-graft chain-length ratio causes aggregation when these variables are independently controlled.
status: Koh et al.’s 2020 simulations of roughly 5 nm particles show no demixing at chain-length ratio ten without suitable attractions, whereas experiments on roughly 10–20 nm particles commonly demix above ratios around four. Introducing chemical-mismatch interactions reproduces behavior otherwise attributed to autophobicity.
why: Resolving the attribution would replace empirical compatibility rules with reliable nanocomposite design.
key_works: C. Koh, G. S. Grest, and S. K. Kumar (2020), “Assembly of Polymer-Grafted Nanoparticles in Polymer Matrices,” [DOI:10.1021/acsnano.0c05495](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.0c05495).

title: Entanglement threshold for nanotetrapod-promoted polymer flow
open: Determine the molecular-weight and entanglement-density crossover at which dispersed nanotetrapods lower polymer viscosity, including dependence on arm length and loading. Validate the crossover through independently measured chain dynamics across matched polymer series.
status: A 2025 study reports approximately an order-of-magnitude viscosity reduction in ultrahigh-molecular-weight polystyrene, while 9 kDa polystyrene shows no comparable enhancement. The authors identify chain-length dependence as future work and report an approximately tenfold absolute-viscosity discrepancy between dewetting analysis and rheometry.
why: A predictive crossover could make the additive useful across processing conditions while preserving long-chain mechanical performance.
key_works: J. Sarkar et al. (2025), “Nanotetrapods promote polymer flow through confinement induced packing frustration,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63555-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63555-3).

title: Temperature-dependent mechanisms of cellulose hornification
open: Determine which molecular changes cause irreversible loss of cellulose swelling during drying and why water retention and accessible surface change their relationship with drying temperature. Separate kinetic trapping, fibril coalescence, and chemical cross-linking.
status: Hornification has been recognized since the 1940s. A 2023 study frames it as kinetic trapping; 2025 pulp experiments find different water-retention–surface-accessibility correlations below and above 100 °C, supporting multiple mechanisms without uniquely identifying them.
why: Mechanistic control would preserve accessibility through drying for paper reuse, nanocellulose processing, and biomass conversion.
key_works: F. A. Sellman et al. (2023), “Hornification of cellulose-rich materials – A kinetically trapped state,” [DOI:10.1016/j.carbpol.2023.121132](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.carbpol.2023.121132); C. Moser and B. Sjöstrand (2025), “Hornification of Softwood and Hardwood Pulps Correlating with a Decrease in Accessible Surfaces,” [DOI:10.1021/acsomega.5c03470](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.5c03470).

title: Aqueous identity and lifetime of Posner-type calcium-phosphate clusters
open: Determine whether neutral Ca₉(PO₄)₆ clusters are persistent, appreciable solution species under relevant aqueous conditions. Measure their abundance and lifetime relative to protonated and compositionally variable aggregates, without inferring solution structures solely from dried solids.
status: The Posner-cluster hypothesis is longstanding. Revised calcium–phosphate association constants reported in 2024 substantially change speciation predictions; evidence for calcium-phosphate association alone does not uniquely establish the classic neutral cluster.
why: Correct solution species are essential to predictive models of bone mineralization, pathological calcification, and calcium-phosphate precipitation.
key_works: D. P. McDonogh, J. D. Gale, P. Raiteri, and D. Gebauer (2024), “Redefined ion association constants have consequences for calcium phosphate nucleation and biomineralization,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47721-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47721-7).

title: Reproducing enamel crystallites’ defect sandwich
open: Manufacture apatite crystallites with controlled magnesium-rich layers flanking the sodium-, fluoride-, and carbonate-enriched core found in human enamel. Measure gradient-driven residual stress and preferential acid dissolution at matched morphology and overall composition.
status: The 2020 discovery establishes intr crystallite chemical heterogeneity and connects gradients to stress. Enamel-like crystal platforms reported in 2025 improve experimental access, but reproducing the complete gradient and isolating its mechanical–chemical effects remain distinct targets.
why: Gradient-controlled crystallites would clarify nanoscale caries susceptibility and guide restorative minerals.
key_works: K. A. DeRocher et al. (2020), “Chemical gradients in human enamel crystallites,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2433-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2433-3); J. Chang et al. (2025), “Biomimetic Enamel-like Crystals: A Versatile Platform for Unraveling the Basic Mechanisms of Demineralization and Remineralization,” [DOI:10.1021/acsami.5c13544](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsami.5c13544).

title: A falsifiable test of spinorial hastatic order in URu₂Si₂
open: Identify and measure an observable distinguishing spinorial hybridization from competing multipolar explanations of URu₂Si₂ hidden order, including across the pressure-induced antiferromagnetic transition. Explain the symmetry breaking and elusive magnetic signatures with one parameter-consistent model.
status: The parent hidden-order problem dates to 1985. Kornjača and Flint’s 2023 theory unifies candidate hastatic and antiferromagnetic phases and identifies additional vector observables, but remains a discriminating proposal rather than experimental identification.
why: It would establish or exclude an unusual form of spinorial order and constrain correlated-electron hybridization theories.
key_works: M. Kornjača and R. Flint (2023), “Unified theory of hastatic order and antiferromagnetism in URu₂Si₂,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.108.085133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.108.085133).

title: Species-resolved pair breaking by UTe₂ interstitial defects
open: Establish a causal relation between a measured defect species and UTe₂’s transition temperature, residual quasiparticle density, and split transitions. Controlled defect introduction or removal must separate interstitial effects from uranium vacancies, strain, and compositional gradients.
status: Sample dependence has persisted since superconductivity was reported in 2019. Kengle et al. (2025) find interstitial defects in Te2 layers and no uranium vacancies in the examined samples; the resulting explanation needs quantitative, independently controlled validation.
why: It would turn sample quality into a defined physical variable and sharpen unconventional pair-breaking tests.
key_works: C. S. Kengle, N. Schnitzer, M. M. Bordelon, S. M. Thomas, and P. F. S. Rosa (2025), “What causes the variation in superconducting properties of UTe₂?”, [arXiv:2509.20298](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20298).

title: FFLO modulation versus triplet pair-density waves in CeCoIn₅’s Q phase
open: Measure condensate spatial modulation and spin structure directly enough to distinguish an FFLO-modulated d-wave state from one containing a triplet pair-density wave. Reproducing magnetic-domain switching alone does not discriminate theories.
status: The interpretation has been contested since at least the 2014 domain-switching experiment. Gerber et al. infer inhomogeneous triplet pairing; Hatakeyama and Ikeda (2015) reproduce the switching with FFLO modulation and no triplet component.
why: It would identify the pairing response to strong paramagnetic pair breaking in a bulk superconductor.
key_works: S. Gerber et al. (2014), “Switching of magnetic domains reveals spatially inhomogeneous superconductivity,” [DOI:10.1038/nphys2833](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys2833); Y. Hatakeyama and R. Ikeda (2015), “Antiferromagnetic order oriented by Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov superconducting order,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.91.094504](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.91.094504).

title: A phase-sensitive sign test for nodeless CeCu₂Si₂
open: Determine whether the fully opened superconducting gap reverses sign between relevant electronic states using a phase-sensitive junction or calibrated impurity-interference experiment. Discriminate sign-preserving s wave, sign-changing s wave, and matrix-pairing interpretations without assuming the impurity potential.
status: The modern nodeless-gap controversy has developed over the past decade. Zhao et al. (2022) predict a quasiparticle-interference test for s± pairing; the 2023 review documents why a full gap alone does not settle the order parameter.
why: It would resolve a central ambiguity in the first heavy-fermion superconductor.
key_works: S. Zhao et al. (2022), “Revealing sign-reversal s±-wave pairing by quasiparticle interference in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeCu₂Si₂,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.105.014501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.014501); M. Smidman et al. (2023), “Colloquium: Unconventional fully gapped superconductivity in the heavy-fermion metal CeCu₂Si₂,” [DOI:10.1103/RevModPhys.95.031002](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.95.031002).

title: Identifying the one-ninth plateau state in YCOB
open: Determine the order and excitation statistics of the one-ninth magnetization plateau in YCu₃(OH)₆Br₂[Brₓ(OH)₁₋ₓ]. Discriminate Dirac-spinon, chiral topological, and translation-breaking interpretations through thermodynamics, spectroscopy, and disorder dependence.
status: The plateau was reported in 2024. Zheng et al. (2025) measure heat capacity to 41.5 T and 0.46 K and find behavior consistent with fermionic excitations, but the evidence does not uniquely establish topological order.
why: This small plateau provides a precise material test of fractionalization in frustrated magnets.
key_works: S. Jeon et al. (2024), “One-ninth magnetization plateau stabilized by spin entanglement in a kagome antiferromagnet,” [DOI:10.1038/s41567-023-02318-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-023-02318-7); G. Zheng et al. (2025), “Thermodynamic Evidence of Fermionic Behavior in the Vicinity of One-Ninth Plateau in a Kagome Antiferromagnet,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021076](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021076).

title: The dmit-131 residual thermal-conductivity discrepancy
open: Resolve why nominally equivalent β′-EtMe₃Sb[Pd(dmit)₂]₂ crystals yield incompatible conclusions about mobile gapless excitations. A specimen-exchange experiment should quantify thermal contacts, cooling history, disorder, and low-temperature extrapolation on shared samples.
status: Large residual heat conduction reported in 2010 conflicts with two 2019 studies reporting no such term. Kato et al. (2022) test the cooling-rate explanation and find no corresponding changes in structure, resistivity, or NMR; a generally accepted reconciliation remains lacking.
why: The discrepancy determines whether a leading organic spin-liquid candidate carries mobile neutral quasiparticles.
key_works: R. Kato, M. Uebe, S. Fujiyama, and H. Cui (2022), “A Discrepancy in Thermal Conductivity Measurement Data of Quantum Spin Liquid β′-EtMe₃Sb[Pd(dmit)₂]₂,” [DOI:10.3390/cryst12010102](https://doi.org/10.3390/cryst12010102), [arXiv:2201.07073](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07073).

title: The positive thermal Hall mechanism in GdZnPO
open: Identify the excitations producing positive transverse heat transport in honeycomb spiral-spin-liquid candidate GdZnPO. Distinguish transport or scattering by spin and momentum vortices from weak anisotropic-exchange effects, reproducing field and temperature dependence quantitatively.
status: Zhao et al. (2025) report magnetic heat conduction down to approximately 50 mK and positive thermal Hall response at higher temperatures. Idealized ordered-state spin-wave models give zero Chern numbers; vortices, weak perturbations, and quantum effects remain possible missing ingredients.
why: It would connect a measured transport coefficient to the topology of a spiral manifold in a real material.
key_works: Y. Zhao et al. (2025), “Itinerant and topological excitations in a honeycomb spiral spin liquid candidate,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63620-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63620-x), [arXiv:2508.18795](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18795).

title: Equilibrium order versus arrested proton disorder in ice XIX
open: Determine ice XIX’s equilibrium proton configuration and configurational entropy separately from kinetically arrested disorder. Use convergent annealing, isotope-controlled calorimetry, and diffraction to establish whether observed partial order approaches a unique equilibrium state.
status: Structural models already exist. Gasser et al. (2024) recover about 25 ± 3% of the Pauling entropy and show strong isotope-dependent kinetics, including small H₂O additions enabling ordering in D₂O samples that otherwise fail to transform under the tested anneals.
why: It would separate thermodynamic residual entropy from kinetic arrest in a defined hydrogen-bond network.
key_works: T. M. Gasser, A. V. Thoeny, A. D. Fortes, and T. Loerting (2024), “Configurational entropy of ice XIX and its isotope effect,” [DOI:10.1038/s41598-024-61250-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-61250-9).

title: Microscopic trigger of light-erased clay hydration hysteresis
open: Determine which microscopic excitation allows near-infrared illumination to release metastable hydration states in swelling clay. Predict the action spectrum, absorbed-power threshold, isotope dependence, and layer-spacing transition while separating local heating from direct excitation of confined water.
status: Teng and colleagues eliminated hydration hysteresis in synthetic Laponite in 2025 using 785 nm illumination with bulk-temperature control. Their measurements support optically activated nucleation; the microscopic energy-transfer channel and wavelength-dependent rate law remain follow-up targets.
why: A mechanism would make optical control of mineral hydration predictable and test how confined water crosses metastable free-energy barriers.
key_works: Y. Teng, C. Chen, L. Zheng, and M. L. Whittaker (2025), “Optically Triggered Nucleation Eliminates Hydration Hysteresis in Swelling Minerals,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c04468](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c04468).

title: Equilibrium versus drying-induced interstratification at the clay swelling crossover
open: Establish whether the mixed nematic, crystalline, and interstratified states between osmotic and crystalline swelling represent equilibrium coexistence or structures selected by drying. Determine their reversibility, phase boundaries, and relaxation times under independently controlled water activity and counterion composition.
status: Hotton and colleagues followed the complete crossover in levitated beidellite droplets in 2025. Layer separations decreased continuously to approximately 30 Å before entering a mixed regime; determining equilibrium versus protocol-dependent selection is a further question arising from the continuously drying geometry.
why: It would establish when clay water-retention curves describe equilibrium and when they encode processing history.
key_works: C. Hotton, T. Bizien, C. Hamon, É. Ferrage, and E. Paineau (2025), “Bridging the Gap between Osmotic and Crystalline Swelling in 2D Layered Materials Using Levitated Droplets,” [DOI:10.1002/smll.202505038](https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.202505038).

title: Experimental proton conduction along montmorillonite edges
open: Measure proton transport specifically along hydrated montmorillonite edges, separating it from interlayer conduction and dissolved-electrolyte transport. Test the predicted dependence on pH, magnesium substitution, edge connectivity, and hydrogen–deuterium exchange.
status: Feng and colleagues’ 2026 simulations found direct and water-assisted proton transfer along clay edges, with connectivity and barriers controlled by local chemistry. Nanosecond molecular trajectories establish a candidate mechanism; whether these exchanges generate a measurable edge-specific conduction channel remains experimentally unresolved.
why: It would connect mineral acid–base chemistry to macroscopic electrical transport.
key_works: Y. Feng, X. R. Advincula, H. Fang, and C. Schran (2026), “Clay Edges Are Dynamic Proton-Conducting Networks Modulated by Structure and pH,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c03748](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c03748); [arXiv:2508.15401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15401).

title: Dissolved-gas enhancement of compacted-clay swelling pressure
open: Test whether dissolved gases increase clay swelling pressure through preferential interlayer partitioning when water activity, external pressure, and counterion chemistry are fixed. Separate this contribution from bubbles, desaturation, and gas-induced chemical reactions.
status: Owusu and colleagues’ 2026 molecular simulations predict gas-dependent pressure increases reaching approximately 1.5 MPa under their modeled conditions. This is a calculated increment; its contribution to the response of a compacted specimen containing both interlayer and interparticle porosity still requires experimental isolation.
why: It would improve predictions for gas-generating waste barriers and underground gas-storage seals.
key_works: J. P. Owusu, K. Karalis, N. I. Prasianakis, A. Ferrari, and S. V. Churakov (2026), “Swelling of Na-montmorillonite in the presence of dissolved gas molecules,” [DOI:10.1016/j.clay.2025.108058](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clay.2025.108058).

title: Location and fate of tetrahedral iron during ferrihydrite aging
open: Locate tetrahedrally coordinated Fe(III) within ferrihydrite and identify the rearrangements that reduce its population during aging. Distinguish particle-interior motifs, hydrated surface sites, and defects, and establish whether dehydration causes the coordination change.
status: Sassi and colleagues compared fresh ferrihydrite with material aged for five years in a 2024 study. Spectroscopy linked aging and dehydration to a decreasing tetrahedral-to-octahedral iron ratio, but the measurements do not uniquely locate the sites or establish the atomic transformation pathway.
why: Site assignments would improve predictions of contaminant binding, iron exchange, and mineral transformation.
key_works: M. Sassi et al. (2024), “Influence of time and ageing conditions on the properties of ferrihydrite,” [DOI:10.1039/D3EN00828B](https://doi.org/10.1039/D3EN00828B).

title: Operando charge compensation and branch selection in vivianite oxidation
open: Resolve how electron loss, water deprotonation, hydrogen defects, and lattice rearrangement couple during hydrated vivianite oxidation. Explain which conditions select a metavivianite intermediate and which bypass it, using simultaneous iron-valence, proton-release, and structural measurements.
status: Sassi and Rosso’s 2025 calculations predict metavivianite stabilization over an intermediate range of approximately 66–33% residual Fe(II). Chiba and colleagues experimentally demonstrated oxidation paths bypassing metavivianite in 2020; the remaining question is conditional pathway selection and charge compensation.
why: It would clarify phosphorus retention and the stability of recovered iron-phosphate products.
key_works: M. Sassi and K. M. Rosso (2025), “Insights into the Oxidation Mechanism of Vivianite to Metavivianite from First-Principles Calculations,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c07790](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c07790); K. Chiba et al. (2020), “The synthesis of metavivianite and the oxidation sequence of vivianite,” [DOI:10.2465/jmps.200417](https://doi.org/10.2465/jmps.200417).

title: Atomic identity of clay-stabilized labile Fe(III)
open: Identify the coordination, nuclearity, and location of reactive Fe(III) retained when montmorillonite modifies Fe(II)-catalyzed ferrihydrite transformation. Measure exchange between interlayer species, external adsorption sites, and nascent iron-oxide structures.
status: Wei and colleagues showed in 2025 that clay–ferrihydrite interactions alter recrystallization and can suppress magnetite formation while retaining reactive iron. Selective extraction establishes an operationally defined labile fraction; assigning that fraction to specific molecular species is the narrower remaining target.
why: It would connect measured reactive-iron inventories to mechanisms of contaminant mobilization.
key_works: H. Wei et al. (2025), “Nano-Scale Insights into Clay Minerals Regulating the Fe(II)-Catalyzed Ferrihydrite Transformation under Anoxic Conditions,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c11232](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c11232).

title: Electron acceptor in emerald-green photooxidation
open: Identify the electron acceptor and reaction sequence that convert arsenic(III) to arsenic(V) in illuminated emerald-green pigment. Close electron and atom balances among oxygen, acetate ligands, possible transient Cu(I), arsenolite, and the final arsenic(V)-rich material.
status: Carboni Marri and colleagues established distinct light- and humidity-driven degradation pathways in 2025. Their paper explicitly leaves the oxidative reaction partner and intermediate sequence unresolved; predominantly Cu(II) final products cannot establish whether transient Cu(I) participates.
why: Identifying the partner would reveal which environmental or binder controls can suppress arsenic migration.
key_works: S. Carboni Marri et al. (2025), “Discovering the dual degradation pathway of emerald green in oil paints: The effects of light and humidity,” [DOI:10.1126/sciadv.ady1807](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.ady1807).

title: Dark dissolution versus photocorrosion in cadmium–zinc sulfide pigments
open: Quantify the fractions of Cd–Zn sulfide pigment loss caused by dark dissolution and light-driven oxidation inside aged paint. Close metal and sulfur balances while independently controlling composition, polymorph, particle size, water activity, and binder ligands.
status: Castagnotto and colleagues’ 2025 study found strong light-driven activity in nanosized cubic compositions containing 20% or 40% zinc, together with lower but measurable dark ion release. The unresolved extension is quantitative pathway partitioning within a binder-confined historical paint layer.
why: It would establish whether limiting light addresses the dominant degradation route.
key_works: E. Castagnotto, S. Alberti, M. Campolucci, P. Manfrinetti, M. Ferretti, and F. Locardi (2025), “Photocorrosion Stability of CdxZn1–xS Yellow-Orange Pigments,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c03274](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c03274).

title: Interdiffusion-driven cavitation inside liquid solder pockets
open: Determine whether interdiffusion-induced tension nucleates cavities inside liquid solder before the liquid is consumed. Distinguish this mechanism from expansion of oxide films or entrained defects and from vacancy-driven voiding in solid intermetallics.
status: Kuziora and Aasmundtveit’s 2025 model predicts a cavitation criterion near −29 MPa for one 5 μm³ Ni–Sn solder pocket, reached after approximately six seconds under specified growth conditions. These are model outputs; actual liquid pressure and the operative void-initiation mechanism remain unmeasured.
why: It would show whether void suppression should target diffusion kinetics, liquid connectivity, or oxide cleanliness.
key_works: S. L. Kuziora and K. E. Aasmundtveit (2025; online 2024), “Solid–Liquid Diffusion Stresses Leading to Voiding,” [DOI:10.1007/s11661-024-07618-y](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11661-024-07618-y).

title: Chunky graphite after high-superheat remelting
open: Explain why remelting low-sulfur ductile iron can produce chunky graphite even during subsequent chill casting. Determine whether its nuclei survive the melt or form anew, separating nucleant memory, magnesium fading, inoculant fading, and carbon supersaturation.
status: Adhiwiguna, Plück, and Deike’s 2025 study found strong thermal-history dependence over 1300–1500 °C remelting conditions. Magnesium and inoculant fading alone could not explain the resulting graphite sequence; disappearance of visible graphite does not establish removal of all heterogeneous precursors.
why: It would make recycled ductile-iron melt treatment more predictable.
key_works: I. B. G. S. Adhiwiguna, L. Plück, and R. Deike (2025; online 2024), “Vermicular and Chunky Graphite Nucleation during Chill Casting: Study on the Dynamics of Ductile Iron Recycling,” [DOI:10.1007/s40962-024-01473-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40962-024-01473-8).

title: Stress-free zero-temperature ground state of PbZrO₃
open: Determine whether ideal, unstrained bulk PbZrO₃ has the conventional Pbam antiferroelectric ground state or a lower-energy ferrielectric arrangement. Resolve nuclear zero-point effects and kinetic trapping with agreement beyond a single density functional.
status: The question sharpened in 2021 when calculations placed competing structures within small energy differences. Ferrielectric–antiferroelectric coexistence was stabilized experimentally through strain in 2024, but strained-film accessibility does not identify the equilibrium zero-stress bulk ground state.
why: The reference antiferroelectric’s actual ground state affects interpretations of switching and energy-storage pathways.
key_works: H. Aramberri et al. (2021), “On the possibility that PbZrO3 not be antiferroelectric,” [DOI:10.1038/s41524-021-00671-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-021-00671-w); Z. Yu et al. (2024), “Room-temperature stabilizing strongly competing ferrielectric and antiferroelectric phases in PbZrO3 by strain-mediated phase separation,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47776-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47776-6).

title: Hundreds-second structural relaxation in magnetocaloric La(Fe,Si)₁₃
open: Determine whether the prolonged structural relaxation after a magnetic-field sweep stops is controlled by intrinsic nonthermal transformation kinetics, thermal lag, or their coupling. Predict the pronounced difference between field-application and field-removal branches using independently measured local temperatures and phase fractions.
status: Time-resolved synchrotron measurements in 2024 found relaxation lasting hundreds of seconds. Free-energy analysis revealed asymmetric barriers and behavior suggestive of nonthermal activation; a mechanism-discriminating account of that inference remains open.
why: Slow structural response can prevent a large equilibrium caloric effect from delivering useful cooling power.
key_works: A. Azevedo Beleza et al. (2024), “Structural dynamics of first-order phase transition in giant magnetocaloric La(Fe,Si)13: The free energy landscape,” [DOI:10.1016/j.mtphys.2024.101388](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mtphys.2024.101388).

title: Reversed odd–even acoustic selection rules in ultrathin lithium niobate
open: Identify the depth-dependent polarization and piezoelectric profile that reverses thickness-mode selection rules in approximately 67 nm lithium-niobate films. Distinguish graded surface damage from domain reversal and predict coupling after controlled surface treatments.
status: Xie and colleagues demonstrated resonances up to 220 GHz in 2025. Even-order modes became dominant as films thinned; surface measurements suggested a graded altered region, with approximately 5–6 nm indicated by reflectivity and approximately 20 nm affected by etching. Its piezoelectric profile remains undetermined.
why: It would enable deliberate sub-terahertz mode selection and identify damaging fabrication steps.
key_works: J. Xie, W. Wu, M. Shen, P. Fay, and H. X. Tang (2025), “Towards terahertz nanomechanics,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63561-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63561-5).

title: Carbon site versus growth-rate origin of the β-Ga₂O₃ 1.6 eV compensator
open: Determine whether the Eᶜ−1.6 eV acceptor in rapidly grown β-Ga₂O₃ is carbon on oxygen site I, carbon on site III, or another growth-correlated defect. Independently vary carbon supply and growth rate.
status: Ghadi and colleagues reported in June 2026 that this state accounts for more than 90% of compensation in their high-growth-rate series.
